events.title: A rover mission reaches Mars
events.description: Pathfinder lands carrying the small Sojourner rover.

events.title: The euro begins
events.description: Eleven countries start sharing a currency for financial transactions. Euro notes and coins will arrive later.

events.title: The September 11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks kill thousands of people in the United States. Families, communities and rescuers face devastating losses.

what_happened_next.text:
One dollar in Apple grew to about $2.86 by April 2002, while Disney ended near 88 cents and Nike near 97 cents. The U.S. share basket gained, though less than Apple. A struggling company can recover in one period, but that does not make every troubled business a bargain. Apple’s endpoint also hides a large fall along the way.

The company stories were different. Nike reported record fiscal-1998 revenue but a nearly 50% drop in net income as weak demand and extra inventory hurt. Disney’s California Adventure opened in February 2001; Disney later said the new resort attractions lifted attendance and hotel stays while adding costs. Apple launched iPod in October 2001, adding portable music to its computer business. These events add context, not a mechanical explanation of the returns.

Pathfinder reached Mars, the euro began for financial transactions and the September 11 attacks caused terrible losses in 2001. People at the April 1997 start could not know this sequence. Apple’s recovery stands out beside Disney and Nike, but even a winning company had steep monthly setbacks. Recognizing a possible recovery and holding through a decline are different challenges.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Tiger Woods’s victory, executive pay and new technology were prominent stories. Apple’s leadership faced criticism while shareholders struggled.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Each company followed its own path. The broad basket spread risk across many businesses, even though it did not match Apple’s large gain.
reflection.what_faded_away: An eye-catching executive pay figure did not forecast five-year returns. A sporting victory did not settle the investment outcome of a sponsor.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The later rankings were unknown. Recognizing Apple’s name today can make its difficult position at the start look less risky than it felt.

hot:1997-04:nike.text: Nike’s fiscal 1998 revenue rose 4% to a record $9.6 billion, but net income fell nearly half to $399.6 million. Weak demand and extra inventory led to discounting, squeezing profit even as sales reached a record.

hot:1997-04:disney.text: Disney California Adventure and two nearby resort additions opened on February 8, 2001. The attractions and hotels brought more visitors and guest spending, but Parks & Resorts operating income fell 2% in fiscal 2001 as costs also rose.

hot:1997-04:apple.text: Apple introduced the iPod on October 23, 2001, a small music player that could hold up to 1,000 songs. It gave Apple a business beyond computers and linked the company’s design and software with digital music, opening a new route to reach customers.
